question: Can the noncontact owner revoke a previously installed SLA reference on fresh native contact evidence before any further grant, and what changes relative to the actual #462 histories?
scope: Archive-only, no new policy forward or physical integration. Keep both timing scenarios of #462, six original teacher episodes, sixteen proposals, and the independently closed V2 noncontact gripper card as a negative control. No controller changes.
stimulus: Use every original 2 ms state.bin.journal contact packet from the first registered query. Bind geometry IDs to that scene; allow only table/cube support (red or blue as present) and four feet/floor. This is the existing V2 raw support rule generalized to its second task cube. The first other geometry contact stops a noncontact owner, regardless of force. Record its geometry pair, measured normal force and preceding integration timestamp. This runs outside the model. Teacher stage and object pose are never consulted to detect contact.
clock: Replay the existing owner with 25-tick grants (50 ms). Inspect the initial query packet, then every 2 ms packet in each completed grant before another effect can be admitted. Register the exact first forbidden packet, the following actual pause at which an owner could cancel, and the remaining ticks in the outstanding grant. Treat missing, invalid, or out-of-order sensor evidence as terminal. A CPU cancel cannot reclaim the elapsed part of a grant or certify native moving STOP.
comparison: Chronological replay of the original 41-point receiver messages in each #462 timing scenario until the earlier of contact, evidence exhaustion, or original terminal. At a tied boundary process fresh contact before an install. Check every prefix wire identity and separate pending returns, accepted sources, and scheduled source motion. Audit a proposed late install/gripper command/grant after terminal, callback HOLD, cleared reference and lack of subsequent publication. For the V2 closed card, retain all 160 original consumed intervals and count false stops across the full 2503..6503 packet range.
